message.content:
You are a sub-agent of the STRUCTURE agent in a clean-room reimplementation project. FIRST read /tmp/structure-agent/BRIEF.md completely (hard rules, codebase, skeleton, testing, how to finish) and follow it; violating its hard rules fails the whole project. (The TYPES part is also done now and merged in the parent's branch: `type`, `types::default_type`, `types::names_for_guids` — the original replaces any string param that is a library entry's GUID with that entry's name before reading params.)

YOUR PART: REBAR and REINFORCE. You own `src/structure/rebar.rs` (+ `src/structure/rebar/` for submodules, declared from rebar.rs) and `src/structure/reinforce/` (its `mod.rs` and any files inside). Scratch work in /tmp/rebar-agent/. Read the `rebar` and `reinforce` specs in `/workspace/executable commands`, the README's Reinforcement row and /workspace/docs/areas/structure-and-mep.md (Reinforcement; Bars by rules; More of reinforce; Bends beyond a hook; The check) closely.

1. `rebar` (`rebar::run`): points [[x,y,z],…] (z over the level), diameter (3 to 100), host (a beam, column, structural column?, footing or floor; the level is then its level), grade (CA-50), layer, closed (a hoop), count (up to 1000) with step [dx,dy,dz], level. Reply (ids), saved JSON, every error and the check order; `rebar::check(pr)` (model rules for bars after every command, found also by hand-editing an original-made .bimcraft); `rebar::element_view(pr, id, x)` (what `elements {"category":"rebar"}` shows beyond the stored fields: length, weight…; the hook is wired). What happens to bars when their host is deleted is EDIT's `delete`, but note what the original does.
2. `reinforce` (`reinforce::run`): everything in the spec and docs — beams (bottom/top rows with `hook` number or {start,end}, `bottom.bent` {count, angle, top}, stirrups with `ends` and `hook`, skin, anchor), columns rectangular and round (bars x/y or count, hook {below, above}, jog {by, from_top, slope}, stirrups — a round one's a 24-gon — ties with hook, anchor), footings rectangular and round (mesh x/y, hook), floors (bottom/top meshes along east and north, hook, stopping a cover short of the outline and of openings, sloped floors following the top with the cover square to it), cover (one number or {top, bottom, sides}; else the host's `Cobrimento` or `ConcreteCover` parameter), grade, grade_stirrup, clearance, `hosts` (all or none, the refusal naming the host; up to 1000 hosts and 20000 bars), `preset` (`crate::styles::presets::find`; given keys replace the preset's key by key; a preset of another kind refused), `check: "NBR 6118"` with `aggressiveness` and `fck` (the `notes`, exact texts), reinforcing again replacing the bars it made (with a layer) and leaving hand-drawn ones, the reply (ids, count, hosts, removed, weight_kg, notes), every error text and the order of the checks (unknown keys with the host named, wrong types — the docs say serde types that deny unknown fields —, what doesn't fit and what to change), and the undo label. Every number in the saved bar paths and the reply must match exactly (float formatting!), so reproduce the original's arithmetic order where results differ in the last digits.
Hosts: beams, columns and footings are made by our build already (`beam`, `column`, `structural_column`, `footing`); floors are ARCH's (in parallel, not in our build): build input projects with the ORIGINAL (`/workspace/executable run --cmd 'floor {...}' --cmd 'beam {...}' --save in.bimcraft`; for sloped floors and openings use whatever the original has: `floor` with a slope, `shaft`…) and run both programs on them (`cmp.py -f in.bimcraft -- run in.bimcraft --cmd 'reinforce {...}' --save out.bimcraft`). Read floor outlines/openings/slopes from the saved floor JSON yourself (a private reader in your files). The test asset /workspace/assets/test_structure_reinforce/rebar.ifc was exported from a scenario that matters: read the IFC text to infer the project and commands behind it and make sure they give identical saved projects.

Test widely with cmp.py, keep regression scripts of many cases in /tmp/rebar-agent/ (sweeps of host sizes, counts, spacings, covers, hooks, angles, jogs, sloped and holed floors, round hosts) and report their pass rates. Commit on your branch and report as BRIEF.md says (include the public functions other areas may want: a bar's length/weight for schedules, deleting a host's bars for EDIT's delete).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. We are reimplementing a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler written
in Rust; README at /workspace/README.md, docs in /workspace/docs, especially
/workspace/docs/areas/structure-and-mep.md, /workspace/docs/areas/families.md, /workspace/docs/disciplines.md),
as a new Rust program built only from observed behaviour. Several agents work in parallel, each owning one
area. Our area is STRUCTURE (`src/structure/`); you own one part of it (your prompt says which files).

## Hard rules (violating any fails the whole project)
- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it (args, stdin, files,
  env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run
  `./compile.sh`.
- No internet; don't look for the program's source anywhere. Rust standard library only (no crates).
- Your code goes ONLY in the files/directories your prompt gives you. Do not edit other files (not even
  `src/structure/mod.rs`, `src/structure/common.rs` or other parts' files); if you truly need a change
  elsewhere, write a private stand-in inside your own files and say so in your final report.
- Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, under `/tmp/<your-part>-agent/`. Commit only Rust.
- Do the work yourself; do not spawn sub-agents.

## The codebase (you are in a git worktree of the repo)
First make sure your worktree has the structure skeleton and the MEMBERS part: `git log --oneline -6` must show
the commits "Structure: module skeleton ..." and "Structure members: ..."; if not, run
`git merge worktree-agent-ae3ecafdd2ebc3dc0` (the parent's branch). The MEMBERS part is DONE and matches the
original: `column`, `structural_column`, `footing`, `beam`, `strip_footing`, `pipe`, `duct`, `conduit`, `cable_tray`,
`wire`, `down_conductor`, `ground_conductor`, `cabling` work in our build (so you may use them in test scripts), with
their model rules and elements view. Its public API (`src/structure/members/`): `geom::run_geom(pr, e)` (axis ends
with absolute z, 3D length, half plumb depth, stands, section, frame()), `geom::run_line(e)`, `geom::section(pr, e)`
(width, depth, round, material), `geom::Justify`, `columns::column_geom(pr, e)` (at, angle, base, top, section),
`column_outline`, and `read::{parse_guid, level_ref, level_param, default_level, level_above, levels,
type_name_param}` — level resolution exactly as the original does it (prefer these to `src/model.rs`, which differs
in corner cases: e.g. the original's no-level text is "the model has no levels"; the level above is the lowest one
more than 1 mm up).
- `src/json.rs`: `Value` (insertion-ordered `Map`; `insert_sorted` for BTreeMap-like maps), serde_json-identical
  parse errors and float formatting (`1e+16`), `to_compact`/`to_pretty`, `.sorted()` (command replies are
  printed with keys sorted, as serde_json::Value), `jobj!{}` macro, `Value::f/u/i/s`, `kind_name()` (serde's
  "invalid type" wording), `fmt_f64`.
- `src/project.rs`: `Project` = `doc` (top-level sections in file order; `insert_top`, `section`,
  `section_mut`, `TOP_ORDER`) + `elements: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (each element a JSON object in the original's
  field order, `guid` first) + `library: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (`{kind, name, guid}`; ids count down from 999999
  via `alloc_lib_id`, never reused in a session; `lib_add(kind, name)`); `alloc_id()` for element ids (from
  `next_id`); `find_guid`, `ids_of(cat)`, `lib_find`, `lib_guid`, `lib_name`, `lib_find_guid`. Elements reference
  each other and library entries by GUID. Family parts (forms, symbols, connectors, wall layers) carry their
  own `id` (counting down with the library ids) and `guid` inside the JSON.
- `src/session.rs`: `Session::execute(cmd, params)`: resolves the command (id or alias, any case), snapshots
  the project, runs it, runs `crate::check::check` (every module's `check(pr)`; ours is
  `crate::structure::check`, which calls each part's `check`), rolls back on any error, records an undo step
  labelled by the command's catalog label when the project changed (or when the command called
  `crate::structure::common::mark_step()`). `s.now_phase`/`s.now_option`: the phase/option new elements get.
- `src/commands/params.rs`: param readers producing the original's texts (`` `x` in mm is required``,

  material_ref(pr, name)` gives a material's GUID by name or GUID; favorites; library). `src/rvt/plan.rs` has a
  planar-faces tracer and `src/rvt/rooms.rs` a room-enclosure test.
- Being written in parallel by other agents (don't implement them; if you need one to build a test input,
  build the input project with the ORIGINAL and load it — see below): ARCH (walls, doors, windows, floors,
  ceilings, roofs, rooms, stairs…), VIEWS, EDIT (modify, move, copy, delete, rename_type, delete_type, purge…),
  READERS (inspect, elements, schedule, and the project-file loader `src/load.rs`, today a plain JSON read that
  is good enough to load the original's files), IFC export/import.

## Our skeleton (`src/structure/`, committed by the parent)
- `mod.rs` (parent's): `dispatch` routes each command id to its part's `run(s, cid, p) -> R<Value>`;
  `check(pr)` calls `types::check`, `members::check`, `family::check`, `component::check`, `rebar::check`,
  `reinforce::check`; `element_view(pr, id, x)` routes per category to `members::element_view`,
  `component::element_view`, `rebar::element_view` — the hook `elements` calls (already wired in
  `src/inspect.rs`, so `elements {"category": ...}` shows what you add); `warnings(pr)` → `family::warnings`.
- `common.rs` (parent's, read-only for you): `R<T>`, `RUN_CATS`, `COLUMN_CATS`, `type_kind(cat)` ("type:beam"),
  `type_path(cat)` (where a category's types live in the file's `types`: structuralcolumn → `structural_column`,
  runs → `runs.<cat>`), `types_of`, `type_of`, `type_guid`, `type_name_of_guid`, `element_type`,
  `add_element(s, e)` (stamps phase/option, allocates the id, inserts; returns the id), `new_guid()`,
  `mark_step()` (make an undo step even if nothing changed).

  project has it, else the first by name) — owned by the TYPES part; others call it.
- The calculators are already listed as read-only in `src/commands/mod.rs::changes_model` (no undo step, no check).

## How to test
`MINE=<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py [-f file_to_copy_into_cwd] [-i stdin_file] -- <args…>`
runs the original and yours in fresh temp dirs and diffs exit code, stdout, stderr and every file written, after
normalising GUIDs (`GUID-N` by first appearance), uids, temp names, IFC GlobalIds and timestamps. Prints SAME or
the diff. E.g. `... cmp.py -- run --cmd 'beam {"points":[[0,0],[5000,0]]}' --save out.bimcraft`.
`run` takes several `--cmd` (each may hold several lines, one `ID {json}` per line), `--script FILE`, and
`--save PATH`; replies are printed sorted and compact, one per line; an error prints `line N (id): message` to
stderr with exit 1. Build with `cargo build --release` (fast). The hidden tests do this same kind of comparison
on many inputs, so match replies, error texts (and the order the checks happen in), saved files (field order,
number formatting: `0.0` vs `0`) and undo labels (`inspect` shows `history`) exactly.
Useful trick: build input projects with the ORIGINAL (`/workspace/executable run --cmd '…' --save in.bimcraft`)
and run both programs on that file (`cmp.py -f in.bimcraft -- run in.bimcraft --cmd '…' --save out.bimcraft`) —
our loader reads the original's files. Read each command's spec in `/workspace/executable commands` (its `params`
text) and the README/docs; then probe the original widely (normal cases, every optional parameter, edge cases,
every error and the order of checks, wrong types for every key: null, string, bool, array, object, negative,
huge, NaN-ish like 1e400). Learn element formats from the original's saved files. Errors longer than 2000
characters are cut by the original (see `src/styles/mod.rs::clip_error`) — check whether that applies to yours.
Write quick regression scripts under /tmp/<part>-agent/ that run many cmp.py cases and report the failures.

## Finish
Commit on your worktree branch (only your files; `git add` them explicitly), with a clear message. Final
message (concise): your branch name and commit; per command what matches and what doesn't (and how widely you
tested it); any stand-ins you wrote for other areas; what other areas must provide or call (public functions you
expose for them, with signatures).

systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
243:| Reinforcement | `rebar` makes reinforcing bars: a round bar of a diameter (3 to 100 mm) and a steel grade (CA-50 unless told) bent along points in mm, in the beam, column, footing or floor it reinforces, which it goes with; `closed` makes a hoop, and `count` with `step` a layer of bars or hoops along a beam. A schedule of rebar lists grade, diameter, length, count and weight (steel at 7850 kg/m³) and, grouped, is a bar schedule. IFC writes and reads each as an `IfcReinforcingBar`, aggregated to its host. The 3D view draws them as tubes (inside their host, so hide it to see them), a section draws the bars it cuts as dots over the poché, and a plan draws each bar of its level as a thin line (solid under the cut plane, dashed over it and under the view range's top, a bar that stands as a dot, bars lying on one another drawn once), hidden with the category. `reinforce` arms a beam, a column, a footing or a floor (round columns and footings, and sloped floors, too) by rules: the engineer gives the cover (or the host's `Cobrimento` parameter) and how many bars, how thick and how far apart (a beam's bars below and above, stirrups with closer ends and hooks, skin bars and anchors; a column's bars on each face, stirrups and ties; a footing's two layers of mesh with their ends turned up; a floor's meshes below and above, stopping short of its outline and openings), and it lays them out inside the cover, checks they fit with room between them and says what to change; a beam's bars and a column's end in hooks if told, some of a beam's bottom bars bend up at each end to the top at an angle (`bent`) and a column's bars step in toward its axis near the top (`jog`); each bar is on a layer, and reinforcing again replaces what it made and leaves bars drawn by hand. `hosts` arms a list alike, all or none (up to 1000 hosts and 20000 bars), and `reinforcement_preset` keeps a named set of the parameters for a kind of host in the project, which `reinforce` takes with `preset` and lets what is given replace. The numbers are the engineer's; `check` "NBR 6118" (with the aggressiveness class and `fck`) adds notes, never a refusal, where the bars made fall short of its usual limits (cover, bar sizes and spacings, stirrups, least and most steel, skin bars), typed from public handbooks and not from the standard's text, so check one against a copy before relying on it. On the desktop, the Structure tab's Reinforce (RF) opens a dialog for the elements selected (any number, of one kind), with the fields of their kind, saying a refusal inside itself, keeping what was typed for the next of its kind, saving the fields as a preset to choose for another and deleting one, and with Remove Bars for the bars it made. Not yet: bends other than a hook, a bent-up bar and a column's jog, round beams, bars beyond a section's cut seen through the concrete. |
362:| Structure tab | Structure > Column (CL on this tab; Revit's own), Beam (BM), Floor: Structural (SB), and Foundation > Isolated Footing (FI), Wall Footing (FW; Revit's FT is Filters here), and Reinforcement > Reinforce (RF, ours: it arms the element selected; RB is the Massing tab's Roof by Face). A beam or a wall footing takes two clicks, or a chain of them (Options Bar > Chain), each step a beam; the Options Bar sets a beam's justification (top, centre or bottom) and its height over the level, a footing's thickness and where its top is, a structural column's height. The tool sketches what the click would make and the beam's length; a beam seen under, over or through the plan is picked by its centre line; Properties shows its Start and End Level Offset, Z Justification and System, and Edit Type its section. A structural floor is the Floor tool with its `structural` flag |
491:| `reinforcement_preset` | | `name?`, `kind?` (beam, column, footing, floor), `params?` (what `reinforce` takes, but the host), `rename?`, `delete?`: a named set of parameters, kept in the project; no `name` lists them |
495:| `reinforce` | | `host` (a beam, a column, a footing or a floor) or `hosts` (a list), `preset?`, `cover?`, `grade?`, `grade_stirrup?`, `clearance?`, and by host: `bottom`, `top`, `stirrup`, `skin`, `anchor` (beam), `bars`, `stirrup`, `ties`, `anchor` (column), `mesh` (footing), `bottom`, `top` (floor), `check?`, `aggressiveness?`, `fck?`: bars by rules, as `rebar` elements on layers, and notes from the check |

content.content:
`fixtures.rs` (original forms, named in the project's language; a fitting or a valve is centred on its pipe, along x, so placing it at the
pipe's height lines them up; a wall device, a board and a luminaire carry their `Mounting Height` in their type, so the Fixture tool
places them at the level and they stand where they hang). The desktop's `mep.rs` has one tool for every fixture and device, `Tool::Fixture(key)`: the families of the
kinds its `FixtureTool` names, listed in its Type Selector and placed as the Component tool places them (`placing` takes the tool's
kinds), and the tabs' ribbon panels; a fixture's two-letter shortcut is in `mep::FIXTURES`, not `SHORTCUTS`, since no command makes
one. Edit Type of a run type also sets whether it is round (a diameter, no depth) and its material.

Reinforcement (`rebar.rs`, `model::Rebar`, `Element::Rebar`, category `rebar`, the `rebar` command; tests in `rebar_tests.rs`). A bar is one
element: a round bar of `diameter` mm (3 to 100) bent along `path` (points in mm, `z` over its level), of steel `grade` (CA-50 unless
told), with the `host` it reinforces (a beam, a column, a footing or a floor, held as a `Guid`, and it goes when its host does). A hoop
is a bar whose last point is its first; a layer of bars, or hoops along a beam, is one command with `count` and `step`, which makes one
element for each (IFC has one `IfcReinforcingBar` for each, and a bar schedule counts them). It has no type: the diameter and the grade
are its own, and the bends are sharp, with no hooks, so its length is the sum of its pieces (`rebar::length`) and its weight that
length of steel at 7850 kg/m³ (`rebar::weight_kg`). Nothing checks that it lies inside its host: `reinforce` places bars inside by construction. The schedule of category `rebar` lists Id, Level, Grade, Diameter,
Length, Count, Weight and Host, and grouped by Grade, Diameter and Length with Count and Weight totalled it is a bar schedule. IFC
writes each as an `IfcReinforcingBar` (`SteelGrade`, `NominalDiameter`, `CrossSectionArea`, `BarLength`) with a body of an
`IfcSweptDiskSolid` along an `IfcPolyline`, aggregated (`IfcRelAggregates`) to its host, or contained in its storey when it has none;
import reads the same back, with the host found by the aggregation. The 3D view draws a tube along each straight piece
(`rebar::tubes`, built with a round run's tube), which the concrete round a bar hides: look at bars with their host hidden. A section draws each bar it cuts as a
dot over the host's poché (`render::section_in` keeps them out of the host's pieces, which would swallow them); a plan draws them too (`render::bar_in_plan`).

Importing a structural program's IFC (Eberick, Cype and the like; tests in `eberick_tests.rs`, written by hand, never from anyone's project). Each
product is named by its mark, so a name that is not its type's (BIMCraft names a product by its type, and writes it as its object type too) is its
`Mark` parameter, for the categories in `import::MARKED` (beams, columns, structural columns, footings, strip footings and floors; not stairs,
which BIMCraft calls "Stair"). The single values of every property set that is not BIMCraft's (`BIMCraft_*`, `RoomSeparation`; `Project Parameters`
is read by its names as written) are project parameters named for the property, a character a formula can't say turned into a space
(`parameter_name`: "Cargas de parede (G2)" is "Cargas de parede G2"), lengths in the file's unit made millimetres; `LoadBearing` is left out because
it already makes a column or a floor structural. The cover Eberick sets (`Cobrimento`, `ConcreteCover`) is therefore on the host as a length, for the
rules that will arm it. A run is found in its body as the way it spreads furthest, except where the body is one extruded profile and the extrusion is
not up: then it runs along the extrusion (`Reader::extrusion`), because a beam between two columns can be shallower than it is deep, and its body then
spreads furthest up. A strip footing, a plan outline stood up, is still read by its shape. A landing slab that belongs to no stair is a floor.

Bars by rules (`reinforce.rs`, the `reinforce` command; tests in `reinforce_tests.rs`). The engineer says how many bars, how thick and how far
apart; the module lays them out in the host's own frame (`Frame`: along, across, up) inside the cover and checks that what is asked fits, with the
message saying what to change. It holds geometry and no standard's table: a spacing or a count is never decided here (that is design), and the
clearance between bars (`clearance`, their thickness and at least 20 mm unless told) is the only rule it brings. Parameters are read with serde types
that deny unknown fields (`Row`, `Pitch`, `Stirrup`, `ColumnBars`, `Mesh`, `Grid`), by key, so a key that is not the host's is refused with the host named.
The cover is `{top, bottom, sides}` (Revit's faces: the top and bottom faces of a beam, a footing or a floor, the ends of a column, and all round
the rest) or one number, and where none is given the host's `Cobrimento` or `ConcreteCover` parameter (a length in mm, as the import of an Eberick IFC
leaves it) is the cover. A spacing is the most between bars: `spread` and `stations` place them evenly from end to end, so the count follows the length
(Revit's Maximum Spacing) and `ends` gives closer stirrups in the first and last `length` mm. A stirrup is a closed loop; with `hook` it runs on past
its first corner to a tail turned into the section at each end (`stirrup`). A beam has `bottom` and `top` rows, `stirrup`, `skin` and `anchor`; a
column `bars` (`x` and `y` along each face, corners counted; a round one, `count` round its circle), `stirrup` (a round one's a polygon of 24 sides), `ties`
(across a rectangular section; with `hook` a tail at each end turned toward the other axis) and `anchor`; a footing a `mesh` of two layers with `hook`
turning their ends up (a round one's bars stop at its circle, `half` in `footing`); a floor `bottom` and `top` meshes (`hook` turning their ends up from the
bottom one and down from the top one, square to the slab's top) whose bars stop a cover short of its outline and of its
openings (`chords`, a scan line through the outline and the openings together; a bar parallel to an opening's edge and nearer it than the cover keeps
its cover from the ends only). A sloped floor's layers are measured from its top face, square to it (`off`, and its secant for the height plumb), so the
cover and the thickness are the type's and its bars follow the slope; a mesh on a slope is one plane's bars. Round beams and strip footings are refused. Each bar is a `rebar` element of the host with a `layer`
(`bottom`, `top`, `skin`, `stirrup`, `bars`, `tie`, `mesh x`, `mesh y`, `bottom x`, `top y`, ...); reinforcing a host again replaces its bars that have a layer
and leaves the ones with none, which were drawn by hand, and one command makes up to `rebar::MAX_BARS`. A bar's layer is in the project file and the
schedule (a field a bar schedule may show), not in IFC. What it does not do: bends other than a hook, laps and splices, bars of a round beam, and any check
against a standard. A section shows a bar in its plane as a strip along it and one it crosses as a dot (the cut of the bar's tube, `section_in`); a bar
beyond the cut stays hidden by the concrete it is in.

More of `reinforce`. `hosts` arms a list (`rebar::MAX_HOSTS`, 1000) alike in one command: every host's bars are made before any is replaced, so one that refuses (its refusal names its category and id) arms none, and `rebar::MAX_BARS_ALL` (20000) caps all of them
together. A `hook` on a beam's `bottom` and `top` rows is the straight leg in mm turned up from the bottom bars and down from the top ones at each end
(a number for both, or `{start, end}`), and on a column's `bars` a leg turned into the section along the way across the face the bar is on
(`{below, above}`); `legs` reads it, with its own words when it is not a length, and a leg that does not stay inside the stirrup (a column's: stop
short of the middle) is refused. The bends are sharp, as every bar's are, and each leg is a piece of the path, so the length and the weight count it.
A `reinforcement_preset` is `reinforce::Preset`, a kind of host (`KINDS`) and the parameters that kind takes, in `Model::reinforcement` and as a library
entry (`Kind::ReinforcementPreset`, so it has an id and a GUID, comes in with Insert from File and is renamed with `rename_entry`); it is checked
for its keys and its size when saved (`Preset::check`, `MAX_PRESETS`) and against a host only when it arms one. `reinforce` with `preset` takes its parameters
and lets any given with it replace them, key by key; a preset of another kind than the host is refused, saying both. Plans: a bar of the plan's level
is drawn from above, solid when the cut plane is over its lowest point and dashed when it is over the plane and under the view range's top, a bar
that stands (a column's) as a dot, and bars that lie on one another (a column's stirrups, one over the next) once.

Bends beyond a hook. `bottom.bent` `{count, angle?, top?}` (`Bent`, `bent_up`) takes `count` of a beam's inner bottom bars (the two at the corners hold the
stirrups and stay straight; the others are picked evenly) and bends them up at each end: along the top face for `top` mm from the end (a fifth of the
length unless told), down a slope of `angle` degrees (15 to 75, 45 unless told) to the bottom row's level and along it. They are on the layer `bent`,
have no hook, count as bottom steel in the check, and are refused where the slopes meet in the middle, where the section is too shallow to rise
in, and where one comes within the clearance of a top bar at the top. `bars.jog` `{by, from_top, slope?}` (`Jog`, `step`, `stepped`) steps a column's
bars `by` mm toward the axis (a corner bar along both faces, a face bar across its own, a round column's radially), the step starting `from_top` mm below
the top and running `slope` mm up for each mm across (6 unless told); the points of the bar above the step move with it, including a hook's leg, and
the bars at their new places are checked against one another for the clearance.

The check (`reinforce/norm.rs`). `check` `"NBR 6118"`, with `aggressiveness` (1 to 4) and `fck` (MPa), makes `reinforce` return `notes`: where the bars
made fall short of the usual limits for the kind of host (Table 7.2's cover by class; for a beam the 4 % most, the 0.15 % least up to C30, skin bars over 600 mm
deep, stirrups of 5 mm to a tenth of the width at most min(0.6 d, 300) apart; for a column bars of 10 mm to an eighth of the side, 4 bars or 6 round,
centres at most min(2 sides, 400), 0.4 to 8 % of steel, stirrups of 5 mm or a quarter of the bars' at most min(200, the side, 12 bars) apart; for a floor
bars of at most an eighth of the thickness at most min(2 h, 200) apart). A note never refuses: an engineer may know better, and the bars are made.
It reads only the bars made, so a limit that needs shear, the load or the aggregate is not in it. The numbers are typed from handbooks and course material
that print them, not from the standard's text, which is paid for, and the item numbers are the 2014 edition's at the level of the chapter's item: check
one against a copy before relying on it. The desktop's Check row (Standard, Aggressiveness class, fck) shows the notes inside the dialog, which stays
open, with the bars made, so a field can change and OK remake them.

The Reinforce dialog (`crates/ui-egui/src/reinforce.rs`, Structure > Reinforcement, RF; tests in `tests/reinforce.rs`). It opens on the one beam, column,
structural column, footing or floor selected (anything else says what to select), with the form of its kind (`BEAM`, `COLUMN`, `FOOTING`, `FLOOR`: tables of
groups of fields, each field the path of the parameter it sets, such as `bottom.count`). Every field is text: a count is a whole number, a bar size is mm,
a length is read in the project's units (`Units::parse`); a field left empty is not sent, a group with none filled is left out, and the command is the one
that says what is missing. OK builds the parameters and runs `reinforce` as one undo step; a refusal is the command's own words, shown inside the dialog
(a status box in the view's corner could lie over its buttons) with the dialog left open and the project unchanged, and a field that is not a number is
named before the command is asked. It takes any number of elements selected, of one form (a mixed selection says so), and arms them with one `hosts` command; Remove Bars removes the bars of all. What was typed is kept for the next element of the same form (not in the project, not on disk). The Preset row lists the project's presets of the form: choosing one fills the fields (`ReinforceDialog::load`, the reverse of `params`, lengths in the project's units), Save Preset keeps the fields as they are under the name typed (`reinforcement_preset`, the parameters without the hosts), and Delete Preset takes the chosen one away; each keeps the dialog open. Remove Bars, shown
when the element has bars the command made (those with a layer), deletes them and leaves the ones drawn by hand. The fields' accessible names are
"Group: Field" (`Bottom bars: Count`), and the cover's is `Cover`, its label having a colon so that no two nodes carry the name.

**Connectors.** A family's `connectors` (`family::Connector`, a list for any discipline; today the electrical device's) say what
a placed device draws: `kind` `power` or `switch`, `system` `power-balanced`, `power-unbalanced` or `switch`, `poles` (1 to 3),
`voltage`, `load_va`, `power_factor` and a `classification`. The numbers are numbers or formulas over the family's parameters, so a
type sets its load (the starter luminaires' `Load` parameter) and an instance parameter lets one component set its own; a
`power-unbalanced` connector's `load_va` may be a list, one load for each pole, and a single number is shared out evenly.
`Family::check` refuses a family of two `power` connectors, a kind and system that don't go together, poles, voltage, power factor
or load out of range for any type, and a load on a switch. A connector is a part (`HasPart`: an id and a GUID, kept by place
while the family is edited), and a family without any reads and places as it always did. A component's `element_json` carries
`connectors` worked out for its type (`Family::connector_values`: `load_va` in all, `load_va_by_phase`), which a circuit will sum;
there are no circuits, panels or fitting-to-pipe joins yet, and the connector holds no position. `Model::warnings` (shown by
`inspect`; `Model::check` stays an error only) says which lighting, outlet or switch family in use holds no connector, so its devices
count as zero load. IFC writes each device with a connector `Pset_ElectricalDeviceCommon` (`NumberOfPoles`, and for a power
connector `PowerFactor` and `RatedVoltage`) and `BIMCraft_Connector` (`System`, `Classification`, `LoadVA`, `LoadVAPhase1`…); IFC
import doesn't read them back.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Hand-edit tests: for each case, apply a python statement to the loaded project dict `d`
(e = d['elements'][ID]) and run the original (and mine with -m) on it with a command.
usage: hedit.py [-m] [-c CMD] base.bimcraft ID 'stmt' ..."""
import sys, subprocess, tempfile, os, json, shutil
exe = '/workspace/executable'
mine = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-add01394c801ae7f2/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
args = sys.argv[1:]
both = False; cmd = 'level {"name":"Zed","elevation":9000}'; post = []
while args and args[0].startswith('-'):
    if args[0] == '-m': both = True; args = args[1:]
    elif args[0] == '-c': cmd = args[1]; args = args[2:]
    else: break
base, eid = args[0], args[1]
for stmt in args[2:]:
    d = json.load(open(base))
    e = d['elements'].get(eid)
    exec(stmt)
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    open(os.path.join(tmp, 'in.bimcraft'), 'w').write(json.dumps(d, indent=2))
    outs = []
    for x in ([exe, mine] if both else [exe]):
        p = subprocess.run([x, 'run', 'in.bimcraft', '--cmd', cmd], cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True)
        outs.append((p.stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1][:400], p.stderr.strip()[:600]))
    print('CASE', stmt)
    for i, (o, er) in enumerate(outs):
        tag = 'ORIG' if i == 0 else 'MINE'
        print('  ', tag, 'ERR' if er else 'OUT', er or o)
    if both and outs[0] != outs[1]:
        print('   *** DIFF')
    shutil.rmtree(tmp)

"""Hand-edit tests: for each case, apply a python statement to the loaded project dict `d`
(e = d['elements'][ID]) and run the original (and mine with -m) on it with a command.
usage: hedit.py [-m] [-c CMD] base.bimcraft ID 'stmt' ..."""
import sys, subprocess, tempfile, os, json, shutil
exe = '/workspace/executable'
mine = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-add01394c801ae7f2/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
args = sys.argv[1:]
both = False; cmd = 'level {"name":"Zed","elevation":9000}'; post = []
while args and args[0].startswith('-'):
    if args[0] == '-m': both = True; args = args[1:]
    elif args[0] == '-c': cmd = args[1]; args = args[2:]
    else: break
base, eid = args[0], args[1]
for stmt in args[2:]:
    d = json.load(open(base))
    e = d['elements'].get(eid)
    exec(stmt)
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    open(os.path.join(tmp, 'in.bimcraft'), 'w').write(json.dumps(d, indent=2))
    outs = []
    for x in ([exe, mine] if both else [exe]):
        p = subprocess.run([x, 'run', 'in.bimcraft', '--cmd', cmd], cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True)
        outs.append((p.stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1][:400], p.stderr.strip()[:600]))
    print('CASE', stmt)
    for i, (o, er) in enumerate(outs):
        tag = 'ORIG' if i == 0 else 'MINE'
        print('  ', tag, 'ERR' if er else 'OUT', er or o)
    if both and outs[0] != outs[1]:
        print('   *** DIFF')
    shutil.rmtree(tmp)

import math, json, sys

def run_frame(start, end, offset, end_offset, justify, depth, elev=0.0):
    dx = end[0]-start[0]; dy = end[1]-start[1]
    h = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)
    dz = end_offset - offset
    length = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz)
    half = depth/2.0*(length/h)
    def ch(z):
        if justify == 'top': return z - half
        if justify == 'centre': return z
        return z + half
    z0 = ch(elev+offset); z1 = ch(elev+end_offset)
    a = [start[0], start[1], z0]; b = [end[0], end[1], z1]
    d = [b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1], b[2]-a[2]]
    L = math.sqrt(d[0]**2+d[1]**2+d[2]**2)
    along = [d[0]/L, d[1]/L, d[2]/L]
    hh = math.sqrt(d[0]**2+d[1]**2)
    across = [-d[1]/hh, d[0]/hh, 0.0]
    up = [along[1]*across[2]-along[2]*across[1], along[2]*across[0]-along[0]*across[2], along[0]*across[1]-along[1]*across[0]]
    return a, along, across, up, L

def pt(o, al, ac, up, t, a, u):
    return [o[i] + al[i]*t + ac[i]*a + up[i]*u for i in range(3)]

if __name__ == '__main__':

An element is made in a phase (its `Phase Created` parameter, the first unless it says) and may be taken down in a later one (`Phase Demolished`), set with `modify {params}`; `now` (a phase, or null) is the phase what this session's commands make is made in (the first phase leaves no value). A view shows a phase and a phase filter (`graphics {phase, phase_filter}`): what's made after it isn't there, what's taken down before it neither, and the rest is new (made in it), existing, demolished (taken down in it) or temporary (both), each shown as its phase filter says (see `phase_filter`). `overrides` ({new|existing|demolished|temporary: override | null}, merged: an override as `graphics` has it, without hidden) is how a phase filter draws what it says overridden; the first two statuses start halftone and dashed red. An element is in an option by its `Design Option` parameter, `set: option`, set with `modify {params}` (a door or window with none is in its wall's); it shows only in a view that shows that option: `graphics {options: {set: option | null}}`. `now` (`set: option`, or null) is the option what this session's commands make is made in. `rename` renames the set, or with `option`, one of its options (elements and views follow). `accept` keeps the primary option's elements in the model and deletes the others' (and the set); `delete` deletes the set and every element in its options. import json, random, subprocess, tempfile, os, math
random.seed(7)
cmds = []
bars = []
for i in range(400):
    d = round(random.uniform(3, 100), random.choice([0, 1, 2, 3]))
    pts = [[round(random.uniform(-5000, 5000), random.choice([0, 1, 3])) for _ in range(3)] for _ in range(random.choice([2, 2, 3, 4]))]
    bars.append((d, pts))
    cmds.append('rebar ' + json.dumps({'points': pts, 'diameter': d}))
cmds.append('elements {"category":"rebar"}')
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
open(os.path.join(d, 's.txt'), 'w').write('\n'.join(cmds) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', '--script', 's.txt'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
out = p.stdout.strip().split('\n')[-1]
els = json.loads(out)['elements']
json.dump({'bars': bars, 'els': els}, open('/tmp/rebar-agent/weights.json', 'w'))

def length(path):
    L = 0.0
    for a, b in zip(path, path[1:]):
        L += math.sqrt((b[0]-a[0])**2 + (b[1]-a[1])**2 + (b[2]-a[2])**2)
    return L

def length2(path):
    L = 0.0
    for a, b in zip(path, path[1:]):
        dx = b[0]-a[0]; dy = b[1]-a[1]; dz = b[2]-a[2]
        L += math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz)
    return L

def length3(path):
    L = 0.0
    for a, b in zip(path, path[1:]):
        L += math.hypot(math.hypot(b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]), b[2]-a[2])
    return L

cands = {
    'A': lambda d, L: math.pi * d * d / 4.0 * L * 7850.0 * 1e-9,
    'B': lambda d, L: math.pi * (d / 2000.0) ** 2 * (L / 1000.0) * 7850.0,
    'C': lambda d, L: (math.pi * d * d / 4.0) * L / 1e9 * 7850.0,
    'D': lambda d, L: math.pi * (d/2.0)**2 * L * 1e-9 * 7850.0,
    'E': lambda d, L: (d/1000.0)**2 * math.pi / 4.0 * (L/1000.0) * 7850.0,
    'F': lambda d, L: math.pi * (d/2000.0) * (d/2000.0) * (L/1000.0) * 7850.0,
    'G': lambda d, L: 7850.0 * math.pi * d * d / 4.0 * L / 1e9,
    'H': lambda d, L: math.pi * d * d / 4.0 / 1e6 * L / 1000.0 * 7850.0,
    'I': lambda d, L: math.pi * d * d / 4.0 * 1e-6 * (L / 1000.0) * 7850.0,
    'J': lambda d, L: (math.pi / 4.0) * d * d * L * 7.85e-6 / 1000.0,
    'K': lambda d, L: math.pi * (d * 0.001 / 2.0) ** 2 * (L * 0.001) * 7850.0,
    'L': lambda d, L: (L / 1000.0) * math.pi * (d / 2000.0) ** 2 * 7850.0,
    'M': lambda d, L: 7850.0 * (L / 1000.0) * math.pi * (d / 2000.0) ** 2,
    'N': lambda d, L: math.pi * (d / 2000.0).__pow__(2) * L / 1000.0 * 7850.0,
}
def r3(x): return round(x * 1000.0) / 1000.0
def rr(x):
    # rust f64::round: half away from zero
    return math.floor(x * 1000.0 + 0.5) / 1000.0 if x >= 0 else -math.floor(-x * 1000.0 + 0.5) / 1000.0
for lname, lf in (('len1', length), ('len2', length2), ('len3', length3)):
    lok = sum(1 for (dd, pts), e in zip(bars, els) if rr(lf(pts) * 100.0 / 1000.0) * 1000 / 100 == e['length'] or math.floor(lf(pts)*100+0.5)/100 == e['length'])
    for k, f in cands.items():

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find the order in which the original reports failures: each failure is a patch to a valid base
params dict; run every pair and see which wins. usage: order.py beam|column|footing|floor"""
import sys, json, subprocess, tempfile, os, shutil, itertools, copy
kind = sys.argv[1]
FILE = '/tmp/rebar-agent/' + (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'hosts1.bimcraft')
exe = '/workspace/executable'

def merge(a, b):
    out = copy.deepcopy(a)
    for k, v in b.items():
        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(out.get(k), dict):
            out[k] = merge(out[k], v)
        else:
            out[k] = v
    return out

if kind == 'beam':
    base = {"host": 100002, "cover": 25, "bottom": {"count": 4, "diameter": 16}, "top": {"count": 2, "diameter": 10},
            "stirrup": {"diameter": 5, "spacing": 150}, "skin": {"diameter": 8, "spacing": 100}}
    fails = {
        'b.diam': {"bottom": {"diameter": 2}},
        'b.count': {"bottom": {"count": 0}},
        'b.hook': {"bottom": {"hook": -1}},
        'b.hookfit': {"bottom": {"hook": 5000}},
        'b.bentc': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 5}}},
        'b.benta': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 1, "angle": 5}}},
        'b.bentt': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 1, "top": -1}}},
        'b.bentmeet': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 1, "top": 3000}}},
        'b.clear': {"bottom": {"count": 9}},
        't.diam': {"top": {"diameter": 2}},
        't.count': {"top": {"count": 0}},
        't.hook': {"top": {"hook": -1}},
        't.hookfit': {"top": {"hook": 5000}},
        't.bent': {"top": {"bent": {"count": 1}}},
        't.clear': {"top": {"count": 12}},
        's.diam': {"stirrup": {"diameter": 2}},
        's.spac': {"stirrup": {"spacing": 1}},
        's.hook': {"stirrup": {"hook": -1}},
        's.endl': {"stirrup": {"ends": {"length": 0, "spacing": 100}}},
        's.ends': {"stirrup": {"ends": {"length": 100, "spacing": 1}}},
        's.many': {"stirrup": {"spacing": 5.5}},
        'k.diam': {"skin": {"diameter": 2}},
        'k.spac': {"skin": {"spacing": 1}},
        'a.start': {"anchor": {"start": -1}},
        'a.end': {"anchor": {"end": -1}},
        'cover': {"cover": 200},
        'clr': {"clearance": -1},
        'grade': {"grade": ""},
        'unk': {"foo": 1},
    }
else:
    raise SystemExit('kind?')

def run(params):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    shutil.copy(FILE, d)
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', os.path.basename(FILE), '--cmd', 'reinforce ' + json.dumps(params)], cwd=d,
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return p.stderr.strip().replace('line 1 (reinforce): reinforce: ', '')

single = {}
for k, f in fails.items():
    single[k] = run(merge(base, f))
    print('%-10s %s' % (k, single[k][:150]))
print('base:', run(base)[:100])
wins = {}
names = list(fails)
for a, b in itertools.combinations(names, 2):
    e = run(merge(merge(base, fails[a]), fails[b]))
    w = [k for k in (a, b) if single[k] and e == single[k]]
    wins[(a, b)] = w[0] if len(w) == 1 else ('?' if not w else 'both')
    if len(w) != 1:
        print('pair', a, b, '->', e[:120])
# order: count how many each beats
score = {k: 0 for k in names}
for (a, b), w in wins.items():
    if w in (a, b): score[w] += 1
for k in sorted(names, key=lambda k: -score[k]):
    beats = [b if a == k else a for (a, b), w in wins.items() if w == k]
    print('%-10s beats %2d' % (k, score[k]))
json.dump({'%s|%s' % k: v for k, v in wins.items()}, open('/tmp/rebar-agent/order_%s.json' % kind, 'w'))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find the order in which the original reports failures: each failure is a patch to a valid base
params dict; run every pair and see which wins. usage: order.py beam|column|footing|floor"""
import sys, json, subprocess, tempfile, os, shutil, itertools, copy
kind = sys.argv[1]
FILE = '/tmp/rebar-agent/' + (sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'hosts1.bimcraft')
exe = '/workspace/executable'

def merge(a, b):
    out = copy.deepcopy(a)
    for k, v in b.items():
        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(out.get(k), dict):
            out[k] = merge(out[k], v)
        else:
            out[k] = v
    return out

if kind == 'beam':
    base = {"host": 100002, "cover": 25, "bottom": {"count": 4, "diameter": 16}, "top": {"count": 2, "diameter": 10},
            "stirrup": {"diameter": 5, "spacing": 150}, "skin": {"diameter": 8, "spacing": 100}}
    fails = {
        'b.diam': {"bottom": {"diameter": 2}},
        'b.count': {"bottom": {"count": 0}},
        'b.hook': {"bottom": {"hook": -1}},
        'b.hookfit': {"bottom": {"hook": 5000}},
        'b.bentc': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 5}}},
        'b.benta': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 1, "angle": 5}}},
        'b.bentt': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 1, "top": -1}}},
        'b.bentmeet': {"bottom": {"bent": {"count": 1, "top": 3000}}},
        'b.clear': {"bottom": {"count": 9}},
        't.diam': {"top": {"diameter": 2}},
        't.count': {"top": {"count": 0}},
        't.hook': {"top": {"hook": -1}},
        't.hookfit': {"top": {"hook": 5000}},
        't.bent': {"top": {"bent": {"count": 1}}},
        't.clear': {"top": {"count": 12}},
        's.diam': {"stirrup": {"diameter": 2}},
        's.spac': {"stirrup": {"spacing": 1}},
        's.hook': {"stirrup": {"hook": -1}},
        's.endl': {"stirrup": {"ends": {"length": 0, "spacing": 100}}},
        's.ends': {"stirrup": {"ends": {"length": 100, "spacing": 1}}},
        's.many': {"stirrup": {"spacing": 5.5}},
        'k.diam': {"skin": {"diameter": 2}},
        'k.spac': {"skin": {"spacing": 1}},
        'a.start': {"anchor": {"start": -1}},
        'a.end': {"anchor": {"end": -1}},
        'cover': {"cover": 200},
        'clr': {"clearance": -1},
        'grade': {"grade": ""},
        'unk': {"foo": 1},
    }
else:
    raise SystemExit('kind?')

def run(params):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    shutil.copy(FILE, d)
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', os.path.basename(FILE), '--cmd', 'reinforce ' + json.dumps(params)], cwd=d,
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return p.stderr.strip().replace('line 1 (reinforce): reinforce: ', '')

single = {}
for k, f in fails.items():
    single[k] = run(merge(base, f))
    print('%-10s %s' % (k, single[k][:150]))
print('base:', run(base)[:100])
wins = {}
names = list(fails)
for a, b in itertools.combinations(names, 2):
    e = run(merge(merge(base, fails[a]), fails[b]))
    w = [k for k in (a, b) if single[k] and e == single[k]]
    wins[(a, b)] = w[0] if len(w) == 1 else ('?' if not w else 'both')
    if len(w) != 1:
        print('pair', a, b, '->', e[:120])
# order: count how many each beats
score = {k: 0 for k in names}
for (a, b), w in wins.items():
    if w in (a, b): score[w] += 1
for k in sorted(names, key=lambda k: -score[k]):
    beats = [b if a == k else a for (a, b), w in wins.items() if w == k]
    print('%-10s beats %2d' % (k, score[k]))
json.dump({'%s|%s' % k: v for k, v in wins.items()}, open('/tmp/rebar-agent/order_%s.json' % kind, 'w'))

"""Fit the beam frame on whole bar paths of the original for given cases (project, beam id, params)."""
import math, json, subprocess, tempfile, os, shutil, sys
def unit(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+v[1]*v[1]+v[2]*v[2]); return [v[0]/l, v[1]/l, v[2]/l]
def cross(a, b):
    return [a[1]*b[2]-a[2]*b[1], a[2]*b[0]-a[0]*b[2], a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0]]
def run_orig(f, cmd):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); shutil.copy(f, d)
    subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'run', os.path.basename(f), '--cmd', cmd, '--save', 'o.bimcraft'], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    j = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft'))); shutil.rmtree(d)
    return j
def frames(dv):
    dx, dy, dz = dv
    L = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz)
    hz = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)
    for an, al in (('al1', [dx/L, dy/L, dz/L]), ('al2', unit(dv))):
        acs = {'dv': [-dy/hz, dx/hz, 0.0], 'al': unit([-al[1], al[0], 0.0])}
        for cn, ac in acs.items():
            for un, up in (('cross', cross(al, ac)), ('ucross', unit(cross(al, ac)))):
                yield (an, cn, un), L, al, ac, up
def main(f, bid, params):
    j0 = json.load(open(f))
    e = j0['elements'][str(bid)]
    lv = [v for v in j0['elements'].values() if v['guid'] == e['level']][0]
    elev = lv['elevation']
    tname = [v['name'] for v in j0['library'].values() if v['guid'] == e['type']][0]
    t = j0['types']['runs']['beam'][tname]
    w, h = t['width'], t['depth']
    p = dict(params); p['host'] = bid
    j = run_orig(f, 'reinforce ' + json.dumps(p))
    bars = [v for v in j['elements'].values() if v['category'] == 'rebar']
    s, en = e['start'], e['end']; off = e.get('offset', 0.0); eoff = e.get('end_offset', off); just = e.get('justify', 'top')
    dx = en[0]-s[0]; dy = en[1]-s[1]
    plan = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); rz = eoff-off; length = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy+rz*rz)
    half = h/2*(length/plan)
    ch = lambda z: z - half if just == 'top' else (z if just == 'centre' else z + half)
    z0 = ch(elev+off); z1 = ch(elev+eoff)
    dv = [dx, dy, z1-z0]
    o = [s[0], s[1], z0 - elev]
    c = params['cover']
    hh = h/2; hw = w/2
    res = {}
    for key, L, al, ac, up in frames(dv):
        def at(t, a, u):
            return [o[i] + al[i]*t + ac[i]*a + up[i]*u for i in range(3)]
        # expected bars: bottom row then top row (no stirrup), straight
        exp = []
        for name in ('bottom', 'top'):
            if name not in params: continue
            r = params[name]; d = r['diameter']; n = r['count']
            a = hw - c - d/2
            ats = [0.0] if n == 1 else [-a + (2*a)*i/(n-1) for i in range(n)]
            u = -(hh - c - d/2) if name == 'bottom' else hh - c - d/2
            for aa in ats:
                exp.append([at(c, aa, u), at(L - c, aa, u)])
        tot = 0; ok = 0
        for b, ex in zip(bars, exp):
            for p1, p2 in zip(b['path'], ex):
                for x, y in zip(p1, p2):
                    tot += 1; ok += (x == y)
        res[key] = (ok, tot)
    for k, v in sorted(res.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0]):
        print(v, k)
if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), json.loads(sys.argv[3]))

import json, pickle, math
data = pickle.load(open('/tmp/rebar-agent/search_beam.cache', 'rb'))
def unit(v):
    l = math.sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+v[1]*v[1]+v[2]*v[2]); return [v[0]/l, v[1]/l, v[2]/l]
def cross(a, b):
    return [a[1]*b[2]-a[2]*b[1], a[2]*b[0]-a[0]*b[2], a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0]]
def ups(dx, dy, dz):
    L = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz); hz = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)
    al = [dx/L, dy/L, dz/L]
    out = {}
    for an, a in (('div', al), ('unit', unit([dx, dy, dz]))):
        for cn, c in (('dv', [-dy/hz, dx/hz, 0.0]), ('al', unit([-a[1], a[0], 0.0])), ('alh', [-a[1]/math.hypot(a[0], a[1]), a[0]/math.hypot(a[0], a[1]), 0.0]),
                      ('alraw', [-a[1], a[0], 0.0])):
            out[(an, cn, 'cross')] = cross(a, c)
            out[(an, cn, 'ucross')] = unit(cross(a, c))
            out[(an, cn, 'crossrev')] = cross(c, a)
        # gram schmidt of z
        z = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]
        k = a[2]
        g = [z[0]-k*a[0], z[1]-k*a[1], z[2]-k*a[2]]
        out[(an, '-', 'gram')] = unit(g)
    return out
score = {}
for key, (e, elev, t, bars) in data.items():
    off = e.get('offset', 0.0); eoff = e.get('end_offset', off)
    if off != eoff: continue
    s, en = e['start'], e['end']; dx = en[0]-s[0]; dy = en[1]-s[1]
    h = t['depth']; w = t['width']; c = 30.0
    half = h/2.0
    just = e.get('justify', 'top')
    z0 = (elev + off - half) if just == 'top' else (elev + off if just == 'centre' else elev + off + half)
    o = z0 - elev
    rows = [('b', 12.5, 3), ('t', 6.3, 2)]
    for name, U in ups(dx, dy, z0 - z0).items():
        ok = tot = 0
        bi = 0
        for (rn, d, n) in rows:
            u = -(h/2 - c - d/2) if rn == 'b' else h/2 - c - d/2
            for i in range(n):
                for pt in bars[bi]:
                    tot += 1; ok += (o + 0.0 + 0.0 + U[2]*u) == pt[2] or (o + U[2]*u) == pt[2]
                bi += 1
        sc = score.setdefault(name, [0, 0]); sc[0] += ok; sc[1] += tot
for k, v in sorted(score.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1][0]):
    print(v, k)

import pickle, sys, math, struct
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import beam_lib as B
data = pickle.load(open('/tmp/rebar-agent/search_beam.cache', 'rb'))
def nudge(x, k):
    b = struct.unpack('<q', struct.pack('<d', x))[0]
    return struct.unpack('<d', struct.pack('<q', b + k))[0]
def score(e, elev, t, bars, half, z0mode=1):
    w, h = t['width'], t['depth']; s, en = e['start'], e['end']
    off = e.get('offset', 0.0); eoff = e.get('end_offset', off); just = e.get('justify', 'top')
    dx = en[0]-s[0]; dy = en[1]-s[1]
    sg = -1.0 if just == 'top' else 1.0
    z0 = (elev+off) + sg*half; z1 = (elev+eoff) + sg*half
    dv = [dx, dy, z1 - z0]
    L = B.length(dv); al = B.normalize(dv); ac = B.normalize([-al[1], al[0], 0.0]); up = B.cross(al, ac)
    F = dict(o=[s[0], s[1], z0 - elev], al=al, ac=ac, up=up)
    c = 30.0; hh = h/2; hw = w/2
    exp = []
    for name, d, n in (('b', 12.5, 3), ('t', 6.3, 2)):
        a = hw - c - d/2
        ats = [-a + (2*a)*i/(n-1) for i in range(n)]
        u = -(hh - c - d/2) if name == 'b' else hh - c - d/2
        for aa in ats:
            exp.append([B.at(F, c, aa, u), B.at(F, L - c, aa, u)])
    ok = tot = 0
    for bb, ex in zip(bars, exp):
        for p1, p2 in zip(bb, ex):
            for x, y in zip(p1, p2):
                tot += 1; ok += x == y
    return ok, tot
for key, (e, elev, t, bars) in data.items():
    off = e.get('offset', 0.0); eoff = e.get('end_offset', off); just = e.get('justify', 'top')
    if off == eoff or just == 'centre': continue
    w, h = t['width'], t['depth']; s, en = e['start'], e['end']
    dx = en[0]-s[0]; dy = en[1]-s[1]
    plan = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); rz = eoff-off; ln = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy+rz*rz)
    ha = h/2.0*(ln/plan)
    good = []
    for k in range(-40, 41):
        hv = nudge(ha, k)
        ok, tot = score(e, elev, t, bars, hv)
        if ok == tot: good.append(k)
    print(key, 'half_a', repr(ha), 'good ulp offsets', good)

    for bb, ex in zip(bars, exp):
        for p1, p2 in zip(bb, ex):
            for x, y in zip(p1, p2):
                tot += 1; ok += x == y
    return ok == tot

for key, (e, elev, t, bars) in data.items():
    off = e.get('offset', 0.0); eoff = e.get('end_offset', off); just = e.get('justify', 'top')

import sys, json, subprocess, os, tempfile, shutil, pickle, concurrent.futures
out = sys.argv[1]
cases = []
for fn in sys.argv[2:]:
    cur = None
    for line in open(fn):
        line = line.rstrip('\n')
        if not line.strip() or line.startswith('#'): continue
        if line.startswith('@file'):
            cur = line.split(None, 1)[1].strip(); continue
        cases.append((cur, line))
def run(c):
    f, line = c
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); shutil.copy(f, d)
    cl = ['/workspace/executable', 'run', os.path.basename(f)]
    for x in line.split(' ;; '): cl += ['--cmd', x]
    cl += ['--save', 'o.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(cl, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    res = {'stderr': p.stderr.strip(), 'stdout': p.stdout}
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft')):
        j = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'o.bimcraft')))
        res['bars'] = [v for k, v in j['elements'].items() if v['category'] == 'rebar']
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return f, line, res
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    results = list(ex.map(run, cases))
pickle.dump(results, open(out, 'wb'))
print(len(results))

"""A Python model of the original's beam bars, with switchable arithmetic, compared to cached runs."""
import json, math, pickle, sys, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/rebar-agent')
import beam_lib as B

def section_offsets(V, w, h, cv, ds):
    """returns functions for: across of bars of diameter d, up of bottom/top rows, stirrup box."""
    hw = w / 2; hh = h / 2
    ct, cb, cs = cv
    m = V['sec']
    if m == 'centre':
        bar_a = lambda d: hw - cs - ds - d / 2
        bot_u = lambda d: -(hh - cb - ds - d / 2)
        top_u = lambda d: hh - ct - ds - d / 2
        st = (hw - cs - ds / 2, hh - ct - ds / 2, -(hh - cb - ds / 2))
    elif m == 'inner':
        a_in = hw - cs - ds; t_in = hh - ct - ds; b_in = -(hh - cb - ds)
        bar_a = lambda d: a_in - d / 2
        bot_u = lambda d: b_in + d / 2
        top_u = lambda d: t_in - d / 2
        st = (a_in + ds / 2, t_in + ds / 2, b_in - ds / 2)
    elif m == 'corner':
        bar_a = lambda d: -hw + (w - (cs + ds + d / 2))
        bot_u = lambda d: -hh + (cb + ds + d / 2)
        top_u = lambda d: -hh + (h - (ct + ds + d / 2))
        st = (-hw + (w - (cs + ds / 2)), -hh + (h - (ct + ds / 2)), -hh + (cb + ds / 2))
    elif m == 'mixed':
        a_in = hw - cs - ds; t_in = hh - ct - ds; b_in = -(hh - cb - ds)
        bar_a = lambda d: a_in - d / 2
        bot_u = lambda d: b_in + d / 2
        top_u = lambda d: t_in - d / 2
        st = (hw - cs - ds / 2, t_in + ds / 2, b_in - ds / 2)
    elif m == 'mixed2':
        bar_a = lambda d: hw - cs - ds - d / 2
        bot_u = lambda d: -(hh - cb - ds - d / 2)
        top_u = lambda d: hh - ct - ds - d / 2
        st = (hw - (cs + ds / 2), -hh + (h - (ct + ds / 2)), -hh + (cb + ds / 2))
    return bar_a, bot_u, top_u, st

def spread(a, b, n):
    if n == 1: return [(a + b) / 2]
    return [a + (b - a) * i / (n - 1) for i in range(n)]

def stations(a, b, sp, V):
    n = max(1, math.ceil((b - a) / sp))
    if V['st'] == 'mul': return [a + (b - a) * i / n for i in range(n + 1)]
    if V['st'] == 'step':
        s = (b - a) / n; return [a + s * i for i in range(n + 1)]

def legs(v):
    if v is None: return (0.0, 0.0)
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)): return (float(v), float(v))
    return (float(v.get('start') or 0.0), float(v.get('end') or 0.0))

def model(e, elev, t, p, V):
    F = B.frame(e, elev, t)
    w, h = t['width'], t['depth']
    cv = p['cover']
    cv = (cv['top'], cv['bottom'], cv['sides']) if isinstance(cv, dict) else (cv, cv, cv)
    ct, cb, cs = cv
    stp = p.get('stirrup')
    ds = stp['diameter'] if stp else 0.0
    bar_a, bot_u, top_u, (sa, su, sb) = section_offsets(V, w, h, cv, ds)
    L = F['L']
    an = p.get('anchor') or {}
    t0 = -an['start'] if an.get('start') is not None else cs
    t1 = L + an['end'] if an.get('end') is not None else L - cs
    at = lambda tt, a, u: B.at(F, tt, a, u)
    bars = []
    rows = {}
    for name in ('bottom', 'top'):
        r = p.get(name)
        if not r: continue
        d = r['diameter']; n = r['count']
        a = bar_a(d)
        u = bot_u(d) if name == 'bottom' else top_u(d)
        rows[name] = (u, d)
        hs, he = legs(r.get('hook'))
        sg = 1.0 if name == 'bottom' else -1.0
        bent = r.get('bent')
        chosen = []
        if bent:
            k = bent['count']; m = n - 2
            js = [(m - 1) // 2] if k == 1 else [int(math.floor(i * (m - 1) / (k - 1) + 0.5)) for i in range(k)]
            chosen = [j + 1 for j in js]
        for i, aa in enumerate(spread(-a, a, n)):
            if i in chosen:
                ang = bent.get('angle') or 45.0
                tp = bent.get('top') if bent.get('top') is not None else (t1 - t0) / 5.0
                zt = top_u(d)
                run = (zt - u) / math.tan(math.radians(ang))
                bars.append([at(t0, aa, zt), at(t0 + tp, aa, zt), at(t0 + tp + run, aa, u), at(t1 - tp - run, aa, u), at(t1 - tp, aa, zt), at(t1, aa, zt)])
                continue
            path = []
            if hs > 0: path.append(at(t0, aa, u + sg * hs))
            path += [at(t0, aa, u), at(t1, aa, u)]
            if he > 0: path.append(at(t1, aa, u + sg * he))
            bars.append(path)
    sk = p.get('skin')
    if sk:
        dk = sk['diameter']; spc = sk['spacing']
        ub = rows['bottom'][0] if 'bottom' in rows else bot_u(0.0)
        ut = rows['top'][0] if 'top' in rows else top_u(0.0)
        n = max(1, math.ceil((ut - ub) / spc))
        ak = bar_a(dk)
        for i in range(1, n):
            uu = ub + (ut - ub) * i / n
            for aa in (-ak, ak):
                bars.append([at(t0, aa, uu), at(t1, aa, uu)])
    if stp:
        s0 = cs + ds / 2; s1 = L - (cs + ds / 2)
        ends = stp.get('ends')
        if ends:
            l = ends['length']; esp = ends['spacing']
            a = s0 + l; b = s1 - l
            if b - a > 1.0:
                ts = stations(s0, a, esp, V) + stations(a, b, stp['spacing'], V)[1:] + stations(b, s1, esp, V)[1:]
            else:
                ts = stations(s0, s1, esp, V)
        else:
            ts = stations(s0, s1, stp['spacing'], V)
        hk = stp.get('hook') or 0.0
        dirv = B.normalize([F['ac'][i] - F['up'][i] for i in range(3)])
        for tt in ts:
            c0 = at(tt, -sa, su); c1 = at(tt, sa, su); c2 = at(tt, sa, sb); c3 = at(tt, -sa, sb)
            path = [c0, c1, c2, c3, c0]
            if hk > 0:
                tail = [c0[i] + dirv[i] * hk for i in range(3)]
                path = [tail] + path + [tail]
            bars.append(path)
    return bars

def compare(V, results, verbose=False):
    ok = 0; tot = 0; badcases = []
    for f, line, res in results:
        if res['stderr'] or 'bars' not in res: continue
        p = json.loads(line.split(' ', 1)[1])
        j0 = json.load(open(f)) if f not in CACHE else CACHE[f]
